brief: A shelf unit rated to hold 50 kg of books, with two drawers.

requirements.evidence: Full bases piece at (-1,0),(0,0),(1,0) with top covers as shelves; half-n bases at (0,1),(1,1).
Two addDrawer drawers on the cut faces of the half-n bases (drawer:0#0,1#cut and drawer:0#1,1#cut).

requirements.requirement: Rated to hold 50 kg of books
requirements.evidence: Not verifiable: the configurator knows nothing about load ratings or printed-material strength. Two book props are placed on the shelves for layout only; no load is claimed.

requirements.requirement: House rules (cap open faces, lock joints)
requirements.evidence: lockJoints applied (5 joint bolts). capOpenFaces refused with MESH_CLASH against the drawer frame, so open faces remain uncapped.

finish.summary: Built a small shelf unit: three full hex bases in a row with top covers as shelves, two half-north bases in front carrying two slide-out drawers, lock joints on, mesh clear, no rule errors. Two book rows are placed on the shelves. The 50 kg rating cannot be verified: the configurator checks fit and collisions only, and the load depends on the printed material, wall and joint strength, which I cannot see. Caps on all open faces were refused (MESH_CLASH with the drawer frame), so 14 faces remain open as an info note.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
